container.help: Define materials properties for gases, soils and the carbonation reaction.

value.help: Thermal conductivity of this gas. Contributes to the effective conductivity weighted by the gas volume fraction. Used only when heat conduction is enabled.
Molar heat capacity at constant pressure. The gas contribution to the mixture heat capacity is assembled as the sum of concentration times this value over the species.

container.help: Define properties of the liquid phase for all materials.

value.help: Thermal conductivity of the pore water. Used only when heat conduction is enabled.

container.help: Define the properties of the carbonation reaction Ca(OH)2 + CO2 -> CaCO3 + H2O. These describe the reaction itself and apply to every soil material. The rate law is second order, r = k_T C_aq (A_s - A_r): first order in dissolved CO2 and first order in the lime remaining above the residual.

value.help: Enthalpy of reaction of lime carbonation, per mole of CO2, in J/mol. Enter a NEGATIVE value: carbonation is exothermic and a positive value would cool the soil. The default -113800 follows from Hess's law on the standard enthalpies of formation at 298.15 K, with liquid product water.

Pre-exponential factor of the carbonation rate coefficient k_T = k_o exp(-E/RT). Calibration parameter. In the rate law r = k_T C_aq (A_s - A_r), k_o multiplies the lime remaining above the residual, expressed per unit total volume. Values calibrated against the earlier solubility-capped law, r = k_T C_aq min(A_aq_sat, A_s*), are not transferable: there k_o multiplied the solubility limit, of order 20 mol per cubic metre of water, against order 1000 mol per cubic metre of total volume here. Refit before use.
Activation energy of the carbonation reaction, in J/mol. Calibration parameter.

Coefficient of the interfacial-area factor a = exp(beta (C_aq - C_aq_atm)), in m3/mol. The factor represents the specific gas-liquid interfacial area, which grows as CO2 is forced into the pore network, and supplies pressure sensitivity that the linear C_aq term cannot. Enter 0 to disable the factor and recover the plain second-order law. The factor is normalised at atmospheric CO2, so a = 1 for a specimen in equilibrium with air and a is large at injection pressures. Beta and the Arrhenius factor k_o are fitted together and are not independent: changing one without refitting the other rescales the rate by exp(beta times the change in C_aq). Calibration parameter.

container.help: Define the physical properties of the soil material.
Define the thermal properties of the soil material.

value.help: Thermal conductivity of the soil solids. Dominates the effective conductivity, since the solids occupy most of the volume. Used only when heat conduction is enabled.

container.help: Define how much lime this soil material carries. Used only when reaction kinetics is enabled in the calculation data. The reaction enthalpy and the kinetics are common to all materials and are set under Reactant properties.

value.help: Defined as a fraction of the weight of solids.

Lime shielded by precipitated CaCO3 and therefore unavailable to react. Defined as a fraction of the lime content. Under the second-order rate law the degree of carbonation approaches exactly 1 minus this fraction, so it fixes the final plateau.
